summary: Nez Perce NF 20-foot pole L-4 lookout, built about 1933 (1934 by one history) and destroyed in 1957; no source describes what remains at the site.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1957; no source describes what remains at the site

access.note: On national forest land; the Idaho Fire Lookouts site files it as a hike-in site

events.note: Forest Service list gives 1933 +/-; firelookout.com and the Idaho site also give 1933; the Forest Lookouts site gives 1934
Administration of the site moved from Bitterroot National Forest to Nez Perce National Forest

evidence.supports: 14 miles south of Moose Creek Ranger Station
evidence.quote: 14 miles south of Moose Creek R.S.
1934: A 20-foot round native timber tower with an L-4 cab constructed.

evidence.supports: 1956 transfer from Bitterroot to Nez Perce National Forest
evidence.quote: The administration of the lookout site transferred from the Bitterroot National Forest to the Nez Perce National Forest.

evidence.supports: Archer Point on the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness list
Archer Point on the Nez Perce list
destroyed 1957 on the Nez Perce list

corrections.proposed: Nez Perce National Forest (Bitterroot National Forest until 1956)
corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts site says administration moved from Bitterroot to Nez Perce in 1956; firelookout.com and the Forest Service Nez Perce list place the site in Nez Perce, the agency that held it when it was destroyed in 1957

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Service list, firelookout.com and the Idaho site give 1933; the Forest Lookouts site gives 1934. Recorded as 1933 with the 1934 date noted.

sources.title: Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness Lookouts (compiled by Cindy L. Schacher, 2014)

notes_for_editor: Built year: 1933 from three sources and a Forest Service list with a +/- tolerance; the Forest Lookouts site gives 1934. Agency correction proposed: the record says Bitterroot, but administration moved to Nez Perce in 1956. The Idaho site records no staffing history, so the story says nothing about staff. No source describes what remains at the site today.
